b: Two requests, filed by Canadian government bodies, industry associations and forest products companies, challenge the US Department of Commerce’s 2024 administrative review of countervailing duties on Canadian softwood lumber products.
Canadian softwood lumber producers are seeking a review of US countervailing duty findings under the US-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) (Image: Unsplash)

Two requests have been filed under the US-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) seeking a binational panel review of the US Department of Commerce’s latest countervailing duty findings on Canadian softwood lumber products.

According to a notice published by the International Trade Administration on 23 Nov 2026, the requests were submitted to the US Section of the USMCA Secretariat on 18 Nov 2026. They concern the final results of the 2024 administrative review of countervailing duties on certain softwood lumber products from Canada.

The first request was filed on behalf of the governments of Canada, Alberta, British Columbia, New Brunswick, Ontario and Quebec, alongside provincial lumber trade councils and several Canadian forest products companies.

These include the Alberta Softwood Lumber Trade Council, BC Lumber Trade Council, Canfor, Interfor, EACOM Timber Corporation, Chaleur Forest Products, J.D. Irving, Tolko Industries, Gilbert Smith Forest Products and West Fraser.

The second request was submitted by Resolute FP, the Council of the Quebec Forest Industry, the Ontario Forest Industries Association and their respective members, as well as Plaster Rock Lumber Corporation and CHAP Alliance.
The findings under review were issued by the US Department of Commerce and published in the Federal Register on 19 Oct 2026.

Article 10.12 of Chapter 10 of the USMCA provides a dispute settlement mechanism for reviewing trade remedy determinations made by the governments of the US, Canada and Mexico. Under this process, a binational panel is established to examine the contested determination and issue a binding decision.
Interested parties may challenge the final determination, in whole or in part, by filing a complaint. The deadline for filing is 18 Dec 2026.
Other parties, investigating authorities or interested persons who intend to participate in the panel review but have not filed a complaint may submit a notice of appearance by 4 Jan 2027.
No specific deadline has been set for the panels to issue their decisions.
